problem: It says the hemispherical chamber has "the largest surface area, so heat loss and unburnt hydrocarbon are higher". This contradicts the standard textbook result: for a given clearance volume a dome has the smallest surface-to-volume ratio of the three shapes, so it has the least heat loss and the best thermal efficiency. A student who writes the chapter's version in an exam loses marks.
fix: The dome encloses its volume with the smallest wall area of the three shapes, so heat loss is low. Its real drawback is negligible squish, that is, low turbulence, which slows the burn at part load. (If higher HC is mentioned, link it to wall quenching and poor turbulence, not to "largest surface area".)

problem: "Some syllabi call indirect injection IDI" is redundant and slightly confusing: IDI is already defined in the heading and used throughout the section, so a reader wonders whether it is a different thing.
fix: Delete the sentence, or write: "IDI is the usual abbreviation for indirect injection."

problem: Saying "a bowl that fills about 61 % of the clearance volume is normal for DI" is misleading. In a real DI engine the bowl is nearly the whole clearance volume; the rest is only the thin squish gap, so 61 % is on the low side.
fix: Say: "The bowl holds most of the clearance volume in a DI engine; here it is about 61 %, the rest being the squish gap above the crown."

problem: "A shallow bowl holds the same fraction here as a deeper bowl of smaller diameter" is a coincidence of the two sets of numbers, because the clearance volumes differ (70 cm³ against 55 cm³). As written it reads like a general rule.
fix: Say: "The two bowls give nearly the same fraction only because the clearances differ; in general the volume goes as d² × h, so a given percentage change in diameter changes the volume twice as much as the same percentage change in depth."
